assumptions.summary: Future sea temperature continues the historical trend without sudden shifts, with only bounded fluctuation.
Predators, other environmental drivers, fishing pressure, age structure, and population change are ignored; all fish are temperature-sensitive adults.
An unrefrigerated vessel catches fish, makes no intermediate stop, and returns immediately, so freshness limits the trip.
A refrigerated vessel keeps fish fresh indefinitely and is therefore treated as having no distance limit.
Every vessel works 24 hours per day and 365 days per year without rest, maintenance, weather downtime, or fishing time.
One center-cell temperature is implicitly treated as representative of each whole spatial block.
Temperature preference is treated as the dominant migration driver and omitted habitat variables are held irrelevant.
Fish count is conserved and cell occupancy is used as a distribution proxy rather than an abundance forecast.
Six decadal centroids are assumed sufficient for fourth-order annual longitude and latitude paths.
Every calculated trip lands a full payload at a fixed price, and gross throughput is used as the option-value proxy.

contributions.summary: Separates long-run power growth from annual seasonality and applies the same interface across a 49-block field.
Places a forecast temperature layer inside a species-specific movement automaton.
Runs herring and mackerel through parallel optimum-threshold interfaces and displays their routes.
Connects vessel characteristics and freshness time to port-centered access radii.
Propagates two temperature-trend parameter bundles into migration and port-duration outcomes.
Compares ten Scottish ports across two species and two warming cases.
Reduces decadal CA positions to annual longitude and latitude functions for business calculations.
Maps distance to trip frequency and gross revenue for relocation and refrigeration strategies.
Acknowledges that legal and political effects cannot be quantified with the available model.
Repackages technical findings into a two-page fishing-industry article with dated actions.

data_and_preprocessing.summary: Post-1990 Northeast Atlantic SST observations motivate a rising trend; the paper then fits post-2012 block-center records without publishing the complete data file or station metadata.
The region is divided into 7x7 blocks and each center represents its block; interpolation, coastline masking, CRS, and missing-value handling are not documented.
A red historical series is fitted with six parameters and extrapolated to 2070; time origin and numerical objective are not reported.
Annual averages from daily predictions are assembled into 2030, 2050, and 2070 maps; only one block's coefficients are printed.
The paper reports herring optimum 5.6 C and range -2 to 10 C, and mackerel optimum 6.6 C and range 7 to 17.5 C, with thresholds 0.2 and 0.1.
Initial cells and total population are fixed for the CA, but abundance, age, recruitment, mortality, and calibration data are absent.
A 24 m, 440 kW, 70 t medium fishing vessel and six-hour freshness limit feed speed and range calculations.
Best and worst cases alter only power-trend parameters a, b, and c and report 2070 block temperatures of 7.1 C and 9 C.
Six decadal herring and mackerel coordinate pairs are read from CA outputs and fitted separately in longitude and latitude.
The economic section uses 30 t payload, species prices 444.75 and 883.75, relocation and vessel costs, ten ports, and continuous operation.
MATLAB code hard-codes 18.1 km/h, mackerel price, random option-1 distances, route functions, and an Eyemouth plot; helpers and files are missing.
Only mackerel coefficient tables and ten port coordinates are printed; herring coefficients occur only in code and latitude signs conflict.

independent_extensions.summary: Replace the extrapolative SST curve with benchmarked climate-model ensembles and spatial cross-validation.
Estimate habitat suitability from temperature, depth, salinity, oxygen, currents, prey, and coastline constraints.
Calibrate the CA against tagged-fish or survey distributions and propagate seed ensembles.
Use a geodesic coordinate system and uncertainty-aware trajectory model instead of an absolute-year quartic.
Define freshness as a round-trip clock including search, catch, loading, unloading, and weather delay.
Represent fleet heterogeneity in speed, payload, refrigeration, maintenance, and crew constraints.
Optimize relocation over real candidate ports with access, capacity, transition cost, and delay.
Replace gross throughput with discounted net cash flow including fuel, labor, maintenance, quota, and demand.
Model mixed fleets and staged strategies rather than two mutually exclusive fixed options.
Represent EEZ, quota, licensing, treaties, and enforcement as distinct scenario constraints.
Evaluate warm-water target species with ecology, gear, market, quota, and bycatch data before diversification advice.
Publish complete data, all 49 fits, both species coefficients, code helpers, versions, and deterministic seeds.

judge_relevance_hypotheses.summary: A compact four-part Summary helps judges trace forecast, migration, operations, economics, and public delivery.
Mirroring the three task clauses makes output coverage auditable despite the missing official statement.
Early symbol binding reduces handoff ambiguity across temperature, vessel, and revenue sections.
Shared-time spatial snapshots make the forecast-to-CA handoff quickly inspectable.
A port-species-scenario matrix is decision-relevant when aggregation rules are explicit.
Named options and a switch boundary make recommendations visible, but net-value completeness determines credibility.
Strength-before-limitation ordering preserves contribution while exposing transfer boundaries.
Audience translation is valuable only when scenario labels, uncertainty, and modeled-versus-unmodeled advice remain visible.

models.summary: Estimate one block's long-run SST trend. Map elapsed day through fitted a, b, and c to a slowly increasing baseline.
Represent within-year SST periodicity. Use amplitude p, frequency q, and phase r to produce the seasonal component.
Combine trend and seasonal SST components. Add the power trend and sinusoid to predict daily block SST through 2070.
Instantiate the block 3,3 forecast. Use p=4.194, q=0.0172, r=2.35425, a=1.289e-11, b=2.348, and c=1.399.
Convert optimal-temperature deviation to movement stimulus. Apply a logistic map after subtracting a five-degree offset from the absolute temperature gap.
Advance fish occupancy on a temperature-layered Moore grid. Combine neighbor density, stimulus, random or directed movement, collision checking, and boundaries.
Estimate speed from power, displacement, and length. Scale P/Delta to exponent 0.237 and multiply by square-root length.
Convert freshness duration and speed into range. Multiply six hours by vessel speed and interpret the product as a port-centered radius.
Define lower and higher warming extrapolations. Replace trend coefficients with best and worst bundles while retaining seasonal form.
Interpolate annual fish longitude or latitude. Evaluate a fourth-order polynomial in calendar year; code includes an omitted intercept p5.
Combine fitted longitude and latitude. Package two polynomial outputs as a year-indexed fish coordinate.
Compute annual separation from port to stock. Use coordinate magnitude in prose while code calls a geographic-distance helper.
Convert separation and speed to travel time. Divide twice annual distance by speed, excluding fishing and turnaround time.
Convert trip frequency, payload, and price to revenue. Multiply annual travel-only trips by maximum payload and fixed price.
Aggregate relocation-option value before 2040. Sum 2020-2040 gross revenue and subtract ten relocation costs.
Aggregate fixed-port refrigeration value. Sum 2020-2070 gross revenue and subtract vessel-count times purchase cost.
Measure direct response to speed, payload, and price. Hold two inputs fixed, sweep the third over five values, and compare option curves.

results_trace.summary: The fitted block is reported near 7 C in 2030 and about 9 C in 2070 while preserving a seasonal oscillation.
The paper reports average warming rates of 0.0375 C/year near Scotland and larger rates farther northeast.
The CA sends herring north toward Norway, although the body names Namsos while the Summary and article name Alesund.
Mackerel moves from Scottish waters toward Stavanger and then northwest of Bergen by 2070.
The representative vessel is reported at 18.1 km/h, inconsistent with direct substitution into Equation 6.
Six hours at the reported speed becomes a stated 108.6 km radius and a reported 74,066 km2 area.
Altered trend parameters produce reported 2070 block temperatures of 7.1 C and 9 C.
Table 3 reports port-specific herring and mackerel intervals under both warming cases and highlights Shetland.
The paper summarizes 33 years in the best case and 21 years in the worst case before most ports cannot harvest.
Fourth-order polynomials convert six decadal centroids into annual longitude and latitude estimates.
At Eyemouth and other plotted ports, random-distance relocation has higher computed gross revenue before about 2040.
Once the stock is treated as too distant for relocation, the paper declares refrigerated vessels the only remaining option.
The paper anticipates quota and access pressure near Norway but states that the model cannot quantify the impact.
Higher vessel speed increases both revenues; the refrigerated curve peaks and declines as route distance grows.
Higher payload linearly scales both option revenues and widens their absolute separation.
Higher fish price linearly scales both option revenues by construction.
The paper claims simple forecasting, hybrid temperature-CA coupling, and official data as strengths while listing four simplifications.
The article recommends relocation, refrigeration, quota negotiation, Shetland siting, and warm-water diversification.

unresolved_questions.summary: No separate official 2020 Problem A statement is present in the corpus; task reconstruction therefore relies on the paper's restatement.
Which exact gridded dataset, variables, temporal resolution, and download interval supplied the 49 block series?
What calendar date corresponds to x=0 in Equations 1-4?
What solver, loss, initialization, residual diagnostics, and holdout results were used for each block?
Where are the other 48 block parameter sets and their uncertainty estimates?
Is one temperature block 43 or 50 CA pixels, and how are coast and boundaries handled?
What evidence calibrates the logistic offset, optimum temperatures, thresholds, and population size?
Is the 2070 herring destination Namsos or Alesund?
What output unit and empirical domain does Equation 6 use, and how was 18.1 obtained?
Does six hours cover one-way travel, round-trip travel, or time from catch to landing?
What emissions or climate evidence maps the two a,b,c bundles to best and worst cases?
How are species intervals combined into one no-harvest deadline for a company?
How sensitive are annual coordinates to centroid extraction, polynomial degree, and coordinate metric?
Which actual ports or coastal sites are feasible, and why is relocation modeled by random distance?
How is the requested number of small vessels chosen rather than inserted as a cost multiplier?
What currency year, price unit, relocation cost, vessel cost, and company fleet scope are intended?
Which stocks, zones, quotas, licenses, and bilateral agreements govern each projected route?
Would route, cost, climate, seed, and interaction uncertainty change the strategy ordering?
Which of the five article recommendations are computed, inferred, or independent proposals?
Where are missing herring tables, helper functions, source data, seeds, and environment versions?

weaknesses.summary: Direct substitution P=440, Delta=70, and L=24 into Equation 6 gives about 13.94, not the reported 18.1.
The body labels the reported vessel speed 18.1 km/s, while figures and appendix code use km/h.
Using the printed Equation 6 result, a six-hour range is about 83.6 km rather than 108.6 km.
A 108.6 km circle has area about 37,052 km2, while the paper reports 74,066 km2, almost exactly double.
The stated mackerel optimum 6.6 C lies outside its separately stated survival range 7-17.5 C.
CA prose says each temperature block spans 43x43 pixels, but printed code divides indices by 50.
Printed CA code uses optimalDegree=10.2 rather than the stated herring and mackerel optima 5.6 and 6.6 C.
Printed CA code uses threshold 0.1 only, while the herring parameter table requires 0.2.
Variables run and stop are initialized to zero and never changed, and referenced helpers are absent, so the printed CA cannot reproduce the stated simulation.
Random movement probabilities 0.3, 0.3, and 0.4 are directionally asymmetric rather than an unbiased local walk.
The expression count/8+0.2 can exceed one, so its claimed probability lacks a valid bound.
The route body sends herring to Namsos, while the Summary and public article name Alesund.
Herring and mackerel east-west prose conflicts with the sign and direction of the displayed coordinate changes.
Table 3 labels the Shetland herring duration as 30 even though the printed interval spans 20 years.
Summary values 21.2 and 13.7 are sums of species durations divided by ten ports, not a clearly defined company service deadline.
Equation 10 omits the polynomial intercept p5 that is present in every appendix route function.
Appendix tables disclose only mackerel route coefficients; herring coefficients appear only in code.
Printed appendix latitude-coefficient signs conflict with the corresponding MATLAB functions.
Equation 12 prints a Euclidean coordinate difference while code attempts a geographic distance, leaving metric and units unreconciled.
Option 1 draws uniform random distances without a seed or actual feasible relocation sites.
Relocating every five years through 2040 implies about four events, but Equation 15 subtracts ten relocation costs.
Body equations sum from 2020, whereas appendix revenue code begins its loop in 2021.
Printed business code models only mackerel price and plots Eyemouth, so it does not reproduce both species and all claimed comparisons.
Gross full-load revenue is called benefit despite omitting fuel, crew, maintenance, quotas, fishing time, discounting, and uncertainty.
Option 1's jagged revenue curves are artifacts of independent random distances rather than optimized relocation decisions.
Speed, payload, and price enter revenue proportionally, so their monotone sweeps do not establish whole-model stability.
Territorial sea, EEZ, quota, license, and treaty concepts are conflated in the neighboring-water discussion.
The public article prints team number 207799 instead of 2007799.
The article recommends Shetland, quota renegotiation, and warm-water species without modeling those decisions.
Reference 11 duplicates reference 6 rather than supplying independent support.
Appendix headings are A, B, then A, while the body refers to a nonexistent Appendix C.
The model evaluation contains unreplaced placeholder text 'xx model'.
Only one of 49 block parameter sets is printed, so the full future temperature field cannot be reconstructed.
The long-horizon power-plus-periodic extrapolation has no time-origin disclosure, holdout test, residual summary, or uncertainty interval.
One stochastic CA realization is presented as a most-likely fish distribution without seed ensemble or probability calibration.
A fourth-order polynomial is fitted to only six decadal centroids and evaluated in absolute year without reported conditioning or intermediate-year validation.
